checksum.scope: No checksum is present in these four query/response exchanges.

link.framing: 8N1 receive; two stop intervals on host transmit (8N2 or 1 ms inter-byte gap)
link.notes: libcutter and licut both report 200000 baud, while libcutter explicitly says it needs remeasurement and a separate toolkit reports 198347. Keep the conflict. Do not alter receive to 8N2: receive is 8N1; the second stop interval applies only to host output.

messages.description: 0x12: model ID and two firmware-version components.

fields.encoding: 0x000a Personal, 0x0014 Expression, 0x001e Mini detection-only; other values remain unknown.
fields.name: model_id

messages.name: model_firmware
messages.notes: This five-byte request is the sole executable form. licut's separate comment shows an extra trailing zero; that six-byte documentary inconsistency is not a request variant. See protocol_details.request_width_discrepancy.

messages.name: status
messages.notes: The sole executable request is the five-byte form shown here.

messages.name: mat_bounds
messages.notes: The sole executable request is the five-byte form shown here. libcutter uses 404 internal position units per inch. Boundary origin and per-model interpretation still need stock-hardware confirmation.

messages.description: 0x18: cartridge presence, name region and revision.

fields.encoding: Name region length; version is at body offset 4 + name_offset.
fields.name: name_offset

fields.encoding: Published vector's region: ASCII name followed by NUL and zero padding; decode only before the first NUL.
fields.name: name_region

fields.encoding: Published revision when name_offset is 33; otherwise compute body offset 4 + name_offset.
fields.name: cartridge_version

messages.name: cartridge_info
messages.notes: The sole executable request is the five-byte form shown here. The published response has a 38-byte body, name_offset 33 and version at body offset 4 + 33 = 37. A parser must compute that offset dynamically and bounds-check it instead of trusting it. With no cartridge, present = 0 and name_offset = 0 permit an empty name.

bus.notes: A response begins with one length byte counting only the body, not the length byte itself. It has no opcode echo. Keep one query outstanding and correlate the response with that query. Read until the entire declared body arrives; serial reads may split or coalesce frames. Reject truncated, oversized and trailing data rather than zero-filling it.

discovery.none: Automatic discovery is intentionally disabled. The user identifies the legacy model physically and chooses its serial device. licut's adapter- specific lookup is not a universal Cricut USB identity and is not adopted.

device.name: Cricut Legacy USB Cutters (stock firmware, query only)
device.notes:
STOCK LEGACY USB, QUERY-ONLY. Only model/firmware (0x12), status (0x14), mat bounds (0x11), and cartridge information (0x18) are documented here. No motion, cutting, start/stop transaction, design upload, command key or firmware operation is exposed. Modern Bifrost machines and Explore Air 2 use different protocols and are outside this spec. Replacement-firmware protocols are also out of scope.
Select the exact model and serial port manually. There is no universal USB VID/PID matcher and no blind probing of modern cutters. A serial device belonging to another product must not receive these requests.

openness.notes: libcutter is LGPL-2.1; licut at the reviewed commit has no license grant. This document derives protocol facts and published vectors but copies no licut implementation code or embedded command keys. The legacy vendor software workflow is discontinued, while the machines' stock USB query surface remains useful for identification and preservation.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: USB serial has no pairing mode for this query surface; physical access and manual model selection are the only gate.

exclusivity.notes: The exclusivity is host-side: one process should own the serial port and keep one query outstanding. No device bond is created.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the other serial client and drain stale input before retrying the same benign query. Do not reset the cutter or try motion commands to release a port.

pairing.notes: There is no Bluetooth pairing, network join or application-layer session key for these four queries. Excluded encrypted motion commands are a separate subject and are not part of this spec.

unpair.clears: Nothing; no bond exists. Closing the serial port ends the host association.
unpair.notes: Reset All restores panel settings and is not an unpairing operation.

credentials.notes: The four queries require no account, network credential, pairing key or motion-command key. licut's embedded command keys are not reproduced; libcutter requires owner-provided keys only for excluded motion paths, not for this read-only surface.

factory_reset.description: Reset All is a single physical key press with the machine on. Personal, Create, Expression and Cake have explicit manual procedures. Cake Mini remains an open documentation item rather than inheriting Cake's procedure without evidence.
factory_reset.effect: The physical Reset All key clears the current display and restores panel settings to defaults. It is not a serial command and does not pair, upload or update anything. Cake Mini's Reset All procedure is not established by the manuals reviewed here.

methods.description: Connect a stock legacy cutter by USB, select the exact model and host serial port, then configure 200000 baud 8N1 receive with two stop intervals on transmit. Use 198347 baud only when independent evidence for that unit supports it. Always emit the five-byte implementation request. The six-byte example is only a documentary inconsistency with an extra trailing zero, not a selectable wire form.
methods.name: Manual legacy USB selection and read-only queries

steps.action: Identify the cutter as Personal, Create, Expression, Cake or Cake Mini from its physical labels and manual; do not select Mini, Explore Air 2 or a modern Bifrost model.
steps.expect: A stock legacy model is selected without relying on a universal USB ID.

steps.action: Connect USB and select the corresponding host serial device, excluding other serial equipment.
Open the port for one client at 200000 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit for receive; transmit two stop intervals using 8N2 when supported or a 1 ms inter-byte gap.
steps.notes: 200000 baud is reported by both implementations and explicitly marked for remeasurement by libcutter. Use 198347 only as a separately sourced user override.

steps.action: Issue the five-byte request 04 12 00 00 00 alone, then read exactly its 6-byte body after the length prefix.
steps.expect: Six body bytes decode as model ID, firmware major and firmware minor, all big-endian uint16. A response has no opcode echo, so only one query may be outstanding.

steps.action: If status, mat bounds or cartridge information is wanted, issue the five-byte forms of 0x14, 0x11 or 0x18 separately and validate the exact body length and all offsets before decoding.
steps.expect: Read-only status is returned. No motion, transaction, upload, key or firmware request follows.

troubleshooting.fix: Stop rather than trying other opcodes or the documentary six-byte example. Confirm the physical model and port, drain stale input, verify receive is 8N1 and transmit has two stop intervals, then resolve the unit's baud evidence. Do not automatically switch baud rates.

setup.notes: No account, pairing or network provisioning is needed for the query surface. Physical model and serial-port selection is still mandatory. The user chooses a baud/framing variant only from evidence for that unit; the 200000 versus 198347 baud and five- versus six-byte request discrepancies are not silently reconciled.

rejoin.notes: There is no network binding, pairing or router to rejoin. Moving the USB cable to another host only requires closing the old serial client and manually selecting the correct model/port on the new host.

testing.notes: No stock Cricut was opened, probed or driven. Facts and response vectors are reported from pinned libcutter and licut source and from official manuals. The independent stdlib tests parse the four published response examples, rebuild only the implementation-derived five-byte emitted request form, and reject the six-byte documentary alternative; they are not serial captures.

evidence.open_questions: Nothing here verifies a physical unit. evidence.public_implementation_review: libcutter at d7711ed396aac542781fc4c81dbe6d0eb787b3fd supplied the five- byte writer, model IDs, 200000-baud remeasurement caveat, stop-bit and 404-units-per-inch details. licut at a90f4d735d04df758d0fb385e4967b5daa21058f supplied the four exact response examples, six-byte documentary requests, big-endian response fields, 200000-baud 8N1 receive/two-stop output timing and the implementation's five-byte discrepancy. cricut-re-toolkit at fa09550991380668681a6f20df96d5995fa4de3a supplied the conflicting 198347 value. published_vectors.provenance: The request_hex values are implementation-derived five-byte emitted forms, not exact published requests. Only the four model_firmware, status, mat_bounds and cartridge_info response_hex values are exact licut published response examples, independently decoded here. The no-cartridge response is a synthetic parser boundary vector. Nothing here was captured by this project or is evidence of a live unit.

reported_firmware_compatibility.note: libcutter's broader support table, not this project's hardware verdict and not permission to use its motion path.

request_width_discrepancy.rule: Always emit five bytes. The six-byte example is not a selectable wire form and is never used by the executable messages or test vectors. Do not send both forms or infer a different protocol from a missing response.
request_width_discrepancy.source: licut's response examples show six bytes, while its packet builder and libcutter's fixed command writer both emit five. The sixth byte in the comment is only an extra-zero documentary inconsistency.

response_framing.cartridge_rule: For 0x18, body offsets 0–1 are presence, 2–3 name_offset, 4 onward name bytes, and 4 + name_offset is revision. Require 4 + name_offset < body length. With present = 0 and name_offset = 0, accept an empty name without a terminator. With present = 1, require a NUL-terminated, nonempty ASCII name; absent-carriage names need no terminator.
response_framing.expected_body_lengths_note: Keys are decimal opcodes: 0x11, 0x12, 0x14 and 0x18 respectively.
response_framing.length_prefix: One byte; exact number of following body bytes, excluding itself
response_framing.read_rule: Read the length byte, then exactly that many body bytes. Require the expected length for the outstanding query and reject short or trailing frames. Do not treat a short read as a complete frame.

baud.rule: 200000 is the primary reported configuration; 198347 is a separate toolkit's conflicting value, not a proven correction or fallback. A stock-hardware serial capture is required.
sources: libcutter/libcutter: 200000, with an explicit remeasurement note

serial_discrepancies.inter_byte_rule: licut sleeps 1 ms after each output byte, including the last, to supply the second stop interval while configured 8N1. libcutter alternatively enables 8N2 output and also delays output bytes.

remaining_unknowns: No stock-hardware serial capture establishes whether 200000 or 198347 is correct for a given model/firmware, or why licut's documentary example carries an extra trailing zero. The emitted five-byte request remains the only executable form here.
Create, Cake and Cake Mini model IDs and field-presence/version variation are unestablished; libcutter's support table is reported, not a live query guarantee.
Mat boundary origin and per-model interpretation, and confirmation that every boundary uses the 404-units-per-inch motion scale, need hardware evidence.
Cake Mini's physical Reset All procedure is not established by the manuals reviewed; do not copy Cake's procedure without its manual.
Mini is detection-only in libcutter and its official legacy workflow is defunct; it is not a supported variant.
licut has no license grant found. No code or embedded keys are copied; only derived protocol facts and its published vectors are used.
Explore Air 2, Bifrost, replacement firmware, motion, upload, start/stop and firmware behavior are intentionally outside this spec.
